title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper Addressing Reproducibility Challenges in HPC with Continuous Integration
problem: Artifact evaluation and reproducibility assessment of continuous integration approaches for HPC systems
motivation: Continuous integration tools help address reproducibility challenges in HPC; formal evaluation validates methodology
method: The team followed the SC25 Reproducibility Initiative guidelines to systematically evaluate continuous integration systems used in HPC (high-performance computing—the large-scale clusters that run parallel calculations). They took the code, data, and setup instructions researchers had provided, then tried to rebuild and re-run these systems themselves to see if they could reproduce the published results. They documented what succeeded, what failed, and what crucial information was missing, creating a practical assessment of which continuous integration practices actually work reliably in practice.
key_novelty: This work documents which continuous integration practices for HPC systems are actually reproducible—meaning others can rebuild and rerun them using only the provided code and instructions.
contributions: Artifact evaluation for continuous integration HPC work
Validation documentation for HPC best practices
limitations: Reproducibility reports have limited novelty; focuses on artifact evaluation rather than algorithmic innovation
